children: AMD reported Q3 revenue up 45% to $13.38 billion and adjusted EPS of $2.09, topping estimates. It forecast Q4 revenue near $17 billion; shares rose over 8% after hours.
• Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) forecast faster-than-expected growth in 2027, citing rising data-center sales and revenue. Its shares rose 8% in after-hours trading following the forecast.
AMD agreed to supply Meta with up to $60 billion in AI chips over five years and issued warrants for a potential 10% stake, creating possible shareholder dilution if milestones are met.
AMD said its Helios rack-scale system, powered by MI455X accelerators and Venice server chips, is in production, with output set to ramp in Q4. Meta is testing early systems.
- Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) expects fourth-quarter gross margin of about 55%, down from 56% in the third quarter.
Morgan Stanley raised AMD’s price target to $510 from $465, keeping an Equal-Weight rating; BMO held its Buy rating and $550 target. Susquehanna lifted its target to $650 on Oct. 28.
AMD’s Client and Gaming revenue fell 8% year over year to $3.7 billion. Client sales rose 7% to $2.9 billion, while Gaming revenue dropped 40% to $773 million on lower console component orders.
AMD forecast revenue above analysts’ estimates, while earnings matched expectations, according to Wedbush hardware analyst Matt Bryson.
Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) said it is launching new CPU and accelerator lines and challenging Nvidia with its Helios server design.
AMD unveiled its configurable Helion rack-scale architecture and ROCm 10 software. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure will use sixth-generation EPYC processors in its Compute E7 instances.
